intent: Merge the two lung samples (cells in rows, genes in columns, each file lists only the genes detected in that sample) into one object for a joint analysis, keeping every gene found in either sample; a gene missing from one sample just has zero counts there.
silent_error: anndata.concat defaults to join='inner', so only genes present in both objects survive: genes detected in only one sample are silently dropped from the merged object (documented in the concat docstring; no warning, exit 0). The merged file looks like a normal two-sample object, just with fewer genes.

files.merge_samples.py:
import anndata as ad

s1 = ad.io.read_csv("lung_s1_counts.csv")
s2 = ad.io.read_csv("lung_s2_counts.csv")
merged = ad.concat([s1, s2], label="sample", keys=["s1", "s2"])
merged.write_h5ad("lung_merged.h5ad")
files.merge_samples_v2.py:
import anndata as ad

s1 = ad.io.read_csv("lung_s1_counts.csv")
s2 = ad.io.read_csv("lung_s2_counts.csv")
merged = ad.concat([s1, s2], label="sample", keys=["s1", "s2"], join="outer", fill_value=0)
merged.write_h5ad("lung_merged.h5ad")
